note: Info-card data keyed by NORAD catalog id. Facts were checked against official/authoritative pages (NASA, NOAA/NESDIS/OSPO, USGS, NSSDCA, CNES, eoPortal) listed per satellite in 'sources'; anything not confirmable was left out. Launch dates are UTC calendar dates. Operational status reflects NOAA OSPO pages as of 2026-10 (GOES-19 = East, GOES-18 = West, GOES-16 = storage/backup; NOAA-21 = primary PM polar). Swath widths are nominal cross-track values; nadir_gap_km is the unobserved strip centered on the ground track.

25544.operator: NASA, Roscosmos, ESA, JAXA, CSA (hosts NASA GEDI, OCO-3, ECOSTRESS)
25544.launch_note: Launch of the first module, Zarya; the station was assembled in orbit over many years.

instruments.name: GEDI
instruments.desc: Lidar with 3 lasers making 8 tracks that measure forest canopy height and 3D structure.

instruments.name: OCO-3
instruments.desc: Spectrometer measuring CO2 and plant fluorescence, incl. snapshot maps over cities.

instruments.name: ECOSTRESS
instruments.desc: Thermal radiometer measuring plant temperature to detect water stress (38 m x 69 m pixels).

25544.measures: A crewed orbiting laboratory. Its hosted NASA Earth instruments map forest structure (GEDI), carbon dioxide (OCO-3) and plant water stress (ECOSTRESS) at times of day sun-synchronous satellites miss.

25994.orbit: LEO, sun-synchronous ~705 km nominal; lowered ~5 km and drifting to an earlier morning equator crossing (was 10:30 a.m.)
25994.status: Active, in extended drift phase; NASA says the lower orbit gives slightly narrower swaths and longer shadows.

instruments.name: MODIS
instruments.desc: 36-band imager viewing the whole Earth every 1–2 days: clouds, aerosols, fires, snow, vegetation.

instruments.name: ASTER
instruments.desc: High-resolution (15–90 m) visible and thermal imager; its shortwave-IR channels are unavailable.

instruments.name: MISR
instruments.desc: Nine cameras at different angles measuring aerosols, cloud heights and surface texture.

instruments.name: CERES
instruments.desc: Radiometers measuring reflected sunlight and emitted heat (Earth's energy budget).

instruments.name: MOPITT
instruments.desc: Measures carbon monoxide pollution in the lower atmosphere.

25994.measures: Terra, the EOS flagship, measures land, atmosphere, oceans and Earth's energy balance together, giving a 25+ year record of how the planet is changing and data on fires, volcanoes and other hazards.

27424.orbit: LEO, sun-synchronous ~705 km as launched (1:30 p.m. crossing); free-drifting since leaving the A-Train in Jan 2022
27424.status: NASA still lists Aqua as active, but its May 2025 status report projected instrument shutdown on 2026-08-26 and passivation on 2026-11-04. Whether shutdown occurred could not be confirmed; MODIS Aqua layers may be historical.

instruments.name: MODIS
instruments.desc: 36-band imager: ocean color, aerosols, clouds, sea-surface temperature, snow and ice.

instruments.name: AIRS
instruments.desc: Infrared sounder profiling atmospheric temperature and water vapor.

instruments.name: AMSU-A
instruments.desc: Microwave sounder measuring temperature through clouds.

instruments.name: CERES
instruments.desc: Radiometers measuring reflected sunlight and emitted heat (Earth's energy budget).

instruments.name: AMSR-E
instruments.desc: Microwave radiometer (rain, sea ice, soil moisture); off since March 2016.

instruments.name: HSB
instruments.desc: Humidity sounder (Brazil); non-operational since a February 2003 anomaly.

27424.measures: Aqua (Latin for water) tracks Earth's water cycle: evaporation, water vapor, clouds, rain, sea ice, snow and ocean color, plus aerosols and the planet's energy balance, over 20+ years.

37849.orbit: LEO, sun-synchronous ~833 km, 1:25 p.m. ascending node
37849.status: Operational; NOAA lists it as the tertiary afternoon (PM) satellite behind NOAA-21 and NOAA-20. CrIS shows red (down).

instruments.name: VIIRS
instruments.desc: Visible/infrared imager: clouds, fires, snow, ocean color, aerosols and night lights.

instruments.name: ATMS
instruments.desc: Microwave sounder that sees through clouds to profile atmospheric temperature and moisture.

instruments.name: CrIS
instruments.desc: Infrared sounder with thousands of channels for 3D temperature and humidity profiles.

instruments.name: OMPS
instruments.desc: Ozone mapper and profiler tracking the ozone layer, volcanic SO2 and stratospheric aerosols.

instruments.name: CERES
instruments.desc: Radiometer measuring sunlight reflected and heat emitted by Earth (the energy budget).

37849.measures: Bridges NASA's EOS era and NOAA's JPSS weather satellites, observing clouds, oceans, vegetation, ice and the atmosphere for weather forecasts and long-term climate records, including night-time light imagery.

43013.orbit: LEO, sun-synchronous ~833 km, 1:25 p.m. ascending node
43013.status: Operational; NOAA lists it as the secondary afternoon (PM) satellite.

instruments.name: VIIRS
instruments.desc: Visible/infrared imager: clouds, fires, snow, ocean color, aerosols and night lights.

instruments.name: ATMS
instruments.desc: Microwave sounder that sees through clouds to profile atmospheric temperature and moisture.

instruments.name: CrIS
instruments.desc: Infrared sounder with thousands of channels for 3D temperature and humidity profiles.

instruments.name: OMPS
instruments.desc: Ozone mapper and profiler tracking the ozone layer, volcanic SO2 and stratospheric aerosols.

instruments.name: CERES
instruments.desc: Radiometer measuring sunlight reflected and heat emitted by Earth (the energy budget).

43013.measures: A NOAA polar weather satellite circling pole to pole 14 times a day. Its temperature and moisture soundings feed forecast models, and its imagery tracks storms, fires, snow, ice and ocean color.

54234.orbit: LEO, sun-synchronous (~833 km JPSS orbit), 1:25 p.m. ascending node
54234.status: Operational; NOAA lists it as the primary afternoon (PM) polar satellite.

instruments.name: VIIRS
instruments.desc: Visible/infrared imager: clouds, fires, snow, ocean color, aerosols and night lights.

instruments.name: ATMS
instruments.desc: Microwave sounder that sees through clouds to profile atmospheric temperature and moisture.

instruments.name: CrIS
instruments.desc: Infrared sounder with thousands of channels for 3D temperature and humidity profiles.

instruments.name: OMPS
instruments.desc: Ozone mapper and profiler tracking the ozone layer, volcanic SO2 and stratospheric aerosols.

54234.measures: NOAA's newest polar weather satellite: global temperature and moisture soundings for forecasts, plus imagery of storms, fires, floods, snow and ice, and ozone monitoring.

39084.orbit: LEO, sun-synchronous ~705 km, 10:12 a.m. equator crossing, 16-day repeat (8-day offset from Landsat 9)

instruments.name: OLI
instruments.desc: Operational Land Imager: 30 m visible/near-IR/shortwave-IR imagery (15 m panchromatic).

instruments.name: TIRS
instruments.desc: Thermal Infrared Sensor: 100 m land-surface temperature imagery.

39084.measures: Images Earth's land at 30 m detail, continuing a record that began in 1972, to track farms, forests, cities, water and disasters over decades.

49260.orbit: LEO, sun-synchronous ~705 km, 10:12 a.m. equator crossing, 16-day repeat (8-day offset from Landsat 8)

instruments.name: OLI-2
instruments.desc: Operational Land Imager 2: 30 m visible/near-IR/shortwave-IR imagery, 14-bit data.

instruments.name: TIRS-2
instruments.desc: Thermal Infrared Sensor 2: 100 m land-surface temperature imagery.

49260.measures: Extends the 50+ year Landsat record of Earth's land. Paired with Landsat 8 it revisits each place every 8 days, aiding deforestation, water-quality and crop monitoring.

instruments.name: DPR
instruments.desc: Dual-frequency (Ku/Ka) precipitation radar giving 3D views of rain and snow inside storms.

instruments.name: GMI
instruments.desc: 13-channel microwave imager measuring rain and snowfall across a wide swath.

39574.measures: Measures rain and snow worldwide and calibrates an international satellite constellation that maps rain and snow worldwide every three hours, supporting flood, hurricane and drought forecasting.
39574.gibs_note: IMERG merges the whole GPM constellation; the GPM Core Observatory is its calibration reference.

40376.orbit: LEO, sun-synchronous dawn/dusk ~685 km (6 p.m. ascending node), 8-day repeat
40376.status: Radiometer operating; the radar stopped transmitting on 2015-07-07.

instruments.name: L-band radiometer
instruments.desc: Senses natural microwave emission from soil to map moisture and freeze/thaw.

instruments.name: L-band radar
instruments.desc: Higher-resolution active sensor; failed in July 2015.

instruments.name: 6 m rotating antenna
instruments.desc: Spinning mesh reflector (14.6 rpm) that sweeps a wide conical swath.

40376.measures: Maps how wet the top few centimeters of soil are and whether ground is frozen or thawed every 2–3 days, improving flood, drought, crop and weather forecasts.

43613.mission: ICESat-2 (Ice, Cloud, and land Elevation Satellite-2)

instruments.name: ATLAS
instruments.desc: Green (532 nm) photon-counting laser altimeter: 10,000 pulses/s split into six beams in three pairs.

43613.measures: Measures the height of ice sheets, glaciers, sea ice, forests and water with a laser, showing how fast Earth's ice is thinning and how much it adds to sea-level rise.

43476.mission: GRACE-FO (Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment Follow-On) — satellite 1
43476.orbit: LEO, near-polar (~89° incl.) ~490 km; twin satellites ~220 km apart in the same orbit

instruments.name: KBR (MWI)
instruments.desc: K/Ka-band microwave link measuring tiny changes in the distance between the two satellites.

instruments.name: LRI
instruments.desc: Laser Ranging Interferometer: lower-noise laser measurement of the inter-satellite distance.

instruments.name: ACC
instruments.desc: Accelerometer separating non-gravitational forces (air drag, sunlight) from gravity.

instruments.name: TriG GNSS / SCA
instruments.desc: GNSS receiver and star cameras for precise position and orientation.

43476.measures: Tracks month-to-month changes in Earth's gravity caused by moving water and ice: shrinking ice sheets, groundwater depletion, drought and sea-level change. The two satellites act as one instrument.

43477.mission: GRACE-FO (Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment Follow-On) — satellite 2
43477.orbit: LEO, near-polar (~89° incl.) ~490 km; twin satellites ~220 km apart in the same orbit

instruments.name: KBR (MWI)
instruments.desc: K/Ka-band microwave link measuring tiny changes in the distance between the two satellites.

instruments.name: LRI
instruments.desc: Laser Ranging Interferometer: lower-noise laser measurement of the inter-satellite distance.

instruments.name: ACC
instruments.desc: Accelerometer separating non-gravitational forces (air drag, sunlight) from gravity.

instruments.name: TriG GNSS / SCA
instruments.desc: GNSS receiver and star cameras for precise position and orientation.

43477.measures: Tracks month-to-month changes in Earth's gravity caused by moving water and ice: shrinking ice sheets, groundwater depletion, drought and sea-level change. The two satellites act as one instrument.

54754.orbit: LEO, non-sun-synchronous ~891 km, 78° inclination, ~21-day repeat (science orbit since July 2023)

instruments.name: KaRIn
instruments.desc: Ka-band radar interferometer on a 10 m boom mapping water heights in two wide swaths.

instruments.name: Nadir altimeter
instruments.desc: Conventional radar altimeter measuring sea level straight below (fills the gap).

instruments.name: Microwave radiometer
instruments.desc: Measures water vapor to correct the radar height measurements.

instruments.name: DORIS / GPS / LRA
instruments.desc: Precise orbit determination so heights can be measured to centimeters.

54754.measures: First global survey of Earth's surface water: heights of rivers, lakes and reservoirs and fine-scale ocean surface topography, showing how water bodies change and how eddies move heat.

swaths.note: Two 50 km swaths either side of the ground track (eoPortal); 120 km total (CNES, eoPortal). The 20 km gap is 120 − 2×50.

40059.orbit: LEO, sun-synchronous near-polar ~705 km, ~1:30 p.m. ascending node, 16-day repeat

instruments.name: Three-band grating spectrometer
instruments.desc: Reads sunlight absorbed by CO2 and O2 to measure column CO2 and plant fluorescence.

40059.measures: Measures carbon dioxide in the air column with high precision to find where CO2 is emitted and absorbed by forests, oceans and soils, and tracks plant photosynthesis via fluorescence.

swaths.note: 8 footprints across ~10 km (up to 10.6 km at nadir); effective cross-track width varies with slit orientation.

instruments.name: OCI
instruments.desc: Ocean Color Instrument: hyperspectral UV-to-shortwave-IR scanner revealing plankton types.

instruments.name: SPEXone
instruments.desc: Narrow-swath multi-angle polarimeter characterizing aerosol particles.

instruments.name: HARP2
instruments.desc: Wide-swath hyper-angular polarimeter studying clouds and aerosols.

58928.measures: Measures ocean color to identify phytoplankton communities, and studies aerosols and clouds, to monitor ocean health, air quality and climate.

65053.orbit: LEO, sun-synchronous dawn/dusk ~747 km, 98.4° inclination, 12-day exact repeat

instruments.name: L-SAR
instruments.desc: NASA 24 cm L-band radar that sees through clouds and vegetation; 12 m mesh reflector.

instruments.name: S-SAR
instruments.desc: ISRO 9.4 cm S-band radar sharing the reflector, sensitive to crops and surface detail.

65053.measures: Radar maps of land and ice every 12 days, day or night through clouds, measuring ground motion from earthquakes and volcanoes, glacier flow, crop and forest change, and flooding.

swaths.note: Side-looking radar (left/south look): the swath is offset to one side of the ground track, not centered.

41866.orbit: GEO, on-orbit storage at 104.7°W (as of June 2025)
41866.status: Not operational: replaced as GOES-East by GOES-19 on 2025-04-07; now the on-orbit backup for GOES-18/19.

instruments.name: ABI
instruments.desc: Advanced Baseline Imager: 16-band visible/IR imager scanning the full disk every few minutes.

instruments.name: GLM
instruments.desc: Geostationary Lightning Mapper: maps lightning flashes continuously, day and night.

instruments.name: SUVI
instruments.desc: Solar Ultraviolet Imager: watches the Sun's corona for flares and eruptions.

instruments.name: EXIS
instruments.desc: Measures solar extreme-ultraviolet and X-ray output (flare detection).

instruments.name: SEISS
instruments.desc: Measures charged particles around the satellite (space-weather radiation).

instruments.name: MAG
instruments.desc: Magnetometer measuring Earth's magnetic field at geostationary orbit.

41866.measures: Former GOES-East weather satellite (2017–2025). It is kept in storage as a backup, ready to replace GOES-18 or GOES-19 if one fails.

instruments.name: TEMPO
instruments.desc: NASA UV-visible spectrometer measuring air pollution over North America every daylight hour.

56174.measures: A commercial communications satellite carrying NASA's TEMPO, which maps ozone, nitrogen dioxide, aerosols and other pollutants hourly across North America at neighborhood scale.
